title: Does not work installed signal if in swoole_process run a sleep(1) function
author: optimode

comments.body:
swoole::signal() is based on signalfd and
 eventloop, can not use it in sync blocked server, please use pcntl_signal.

Oh, I understand, thank you. So with swoole i can use pcntl_ functions (eg signal, kill)? Actually, I do not want to use sleep (), it was just an occasional idea.

I would like to develop an email sender application (composer and symfony based) that currently retrieves the data from a redis queue and logs sending data into a mysql database.
What php functions or classes can not I use?

An another question: in php the sleep() function works in the background: 
sleep() -> php_sleep() -> SleepEx() ?
as I know, just system call `sleep`.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why swoole::signal() doesn't work with sleep()
Alternative signal handling approaches that work with blocking operations
Clarification on compatibility between Swoole and standard PHP functions
Technical information about how sleep() is implemented in PHP

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

dockerfile:
FROM php:7.2-cli

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install dependencies for building Swoole
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    git \
    unzip \
    libssl-dev \
    libcurl4-openssl-dev \
    libnghttp2-dev \
    make \
    autoconf \
    g++ \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the repository at the specific commit
RUN git clone https://github.com/swoole/swoole-src.git . \
    && git checkout b0ec90a75ef88a0d5d4cc361fcd972ddecbe4dfb

# Build and install Swoole
RUN phpize \
    && ./configure \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install

# Enable Swoole extension
RUN docker-php-ext-enable swoole

# Create a test file that demonstrates the issue with sleep(1) vs usleep(1000000)
RUN echo '<?php\n\
// Test file to demonstrate issue #2031\n\
// Process with sleep(1) vs process with usleep(1000000)\n\
\n\
// Set up signal handler\n\
Swoole\\Process::signal(SIGUSR2, function($signo) {\n\
    echo "Received signal SIGUSR2 ($signo)\\n";\n\
});\n\
\n\
// Create process with sleep(1)\n\
$process1 = new Swoole\\Process(function(Swoole\\Process $proc) {\n\
    echo "Child process 1 started (using sleep)\\n";\n\
    while (true) {\n\
        sleep(1); // This will block signal handling\n\
        echo "Process 1 iteration\\n";\n\
    }\n\
});\n\
$pid1 = $process1->start();\n\
echo "Started child process 1 with PID: $pid1\\n";\n\
\n\
// Create process with usleep(1000000)\n\
$process2 = new Swoole\\Process(function(Swoole\\Process $proc) {\n\
    echo "Child process 2 started (using usleep)\\n";\n\
    while (true) {\n\
        usleep(1000000); // This will NOT block signal handling\n\
        echo "Process 2 iteration\\n";\n\
    }\n\
});\n\
$pid2 = $process2->start();\n\
echo "Started child process 2 with PID: $pid2\\n";\n\
\n\
echo "Sending SIGUSR2 signal to both processes\\n";\n\
sleep(2);\n\
Swoole\\Process::kill($pid1, SIGUSR2);\n\
Swoole\\Process::kill($pid2, SIGUSR2);\n\
sleep(5); // Wait to observe behavior\n\
\n\
// Clean up\n\
Swoole\\Process::kill($pid1, SIGKILL);\n\
Swoole\\Process::kill($pid2, SIGKILL);\n\
' > test_issue_2031.php

# Set the default command
CMD ["php", "-v"]
